547.hint: The three classical statistical indices representing the central value of a dataset are Mean, Median, and Mode.
547.memory_tip: Measures of Central Tendency = Arithmetic Mean, Median, Mode.

548.hint: Range, Quartile Deviation, Mean Deviation, and Standard Deviation measure dispersion; Median measures central tendency.
548.memory_tip: Measures of Dispersion / Variability = Range, QD, MD, SD; Median is a measure of Central Tendency.

549.hint: Sum the numbers (16 + 18 + 20 + 22 + 24 = 100) and divide by the count of 5: 100 / 5 = 20.
549.memory_tip: Arithmetic Mean = Sum of observations / Number of observations [X̄ = ΣX / N = 100 / 5 = 20].

550.hint: Quartile deviation equals half the difference between the third (upper) and first (lower) quartiles.
550.memory_tip: Quartile Deviation Formula: QD = (Q3 - Q1) / 2 (Semi-interquartile range).

551.hint: The sum of the first 10 natural numbers is n(n+1)/2 = 10(11)/2 = 55. Mean = 55 / 10 = 5.5.
551.memory_tip: Mean of first n natural numbers = (n + 1) / 2 = (10 + 1) / 2 = 5.5.

552.hint: Arrange the scores in ascending numerical order; the middle observation in the sorted distribution is the median.
552.memory_tip: Median = The middle-most value separating the higher half from the lower half of sorted data.

553.hint: Count the frequency of each score: 7 appears most frequently among the numbers.
553.memory_tip: Mode = The score that appears with the highest frequency in a distribution.

554.hint: A pie chart represents parts of a complete circle; the full angle around the center point is always 360 degrees.
554.memory_tip: Pie Diagram: Total sum of angles of all sectors = 360°.

555.hint: Identify the required statistical value (mean, median, or modal score) from the given student marks dataset.
555.memory_tip: Statistical calculations on marks data provide exact central tendency or dispersion values.

556.hint: Karl Pearson's empirical formula connecting the three measures of central tendency in moderately skewed distributions.

557.hint: A graphical representation of continuous grouped frequency distribution using adjacent vertical rectangular bars.
557.memory_tip: Histogram = Graphic bar display for continuous frequency data with no gaps between bars.

559.hint: Apply the semi-interquartile range formula: QD = (Q3 - Q1) / 2 = (80 - 20) / 2 = 60 / 2 = 30.

560.hint: The simplest measure of dispersion computed by subtracting the lowest score from the highest score.
560.memory_tip: Range = Highest Score (H) - Lowest Score (L) [R = H - L].

561.hint: A standard score expressing how many standard deviations a raw score lies above or below the distribution mean.
561.memory_tip: Z-Score = (X - X̄) / SD (Standardized score with Mean = 0 and SD = 1).

562.hint: The mathematical science dealing with the systematic collection, organization, analysis, and interpretation of quantitative data.
562.memory_tip: Statistics = Science of collecting, tabulating, analyzing, and interpreting numerical data.

563.hint: In the grouped median formula L + [((N/2 - CF) / f) × i], the symbol 'i' represents the size of the class interval.
563.memory_tip: Grouped Median: 'i' (or 'c') = Class Interval width / size.

564.hint: In the series 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, every number occurs exactly once with equal frequency; hence no single mode exists.
564.memory_tip: When all observations have identical frequency, there is No Mode (Cannot be determined).

565.hint: Histograms, frequency polygons, and ogives represent statistical data; a Snellen chart tests ophthalmological visual acuity.
565.memory_tip: Snellen Chart = Visual acuity test chart (E chart); NOT a statistical graphical representation.

566.hint: In a frequency distribution table, summing all the category frequencies (Σf) equals the total sample size N.
566.memory_tip: Σf = N (The sum of all frequencies equals total number of observations).

567.hint: Sort the 7 numbers: 9, 24, 35, 43, 53, 76, 80. The 4th middle observation is 43.
567.memory_tip: Median of odd count N: (N + 1) / 2-th term. For N=7, 4th term = 43.

568.hint: Television broadcasts moving dynamic visual imagery accompanied by synchronized acoustic audio narration.
568.memory_tip: Audio-Visual Aids (Edgar Dale) = Television, Sound Films, Video tapes (appeals to both eyes and ears).

580.hint: Educational films stimulate lively peer discussions, shared collaborative analysis, and cooperative classroom learning.

581.memory_tip: Advantage of Educational Films = Bringing distant places, microscopic phenomena, and historical events to life.

582.hint: Arousing curiosity, captivation, and student interest is a tremendous instructional asset, not a drawback or limitation.

583.hint: ICT is an indispensable tool for teachers, providing access to open educational resources and ongoing professional development.
